summary: Martin County steel tower built by CCC Camp P-67 in 1936, with a lookout house and a 1938 garage; no source gives its later history or present condition.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
facts.status_note: No source found says whether the tower still stands.

events.note: Erection of a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower began in April 1936 under the Civilian Conservation Corps and was completed by CCC Camp P-67 on August 8, 1936.
CCC Camp P-67 completed a five-room frame house, 30 by 36 feet, for the lookout man on July 10, 1936.
A combined tool room and garage for the tower was completed on June 22, 1938.

corrections.why: The 1936 construction entry gives a 99-foot 9-inch tower, which is about 30.4 m. No source found gives 30.2 m.

notes_for_editor: All construction dates come from one compiled page that quotes state biennial reports; no separate primary copy was found. Nothing after 1938 found: no condition, staffing, fate or access. Height 30.2 m in the brief is not supported; 99 ft 9 in is about 30.4 m. Not listed on the National Historic Lookout Register. Unverified lead, not used in the story: NGS mark EY0540 (listed near Foreman in the tnlandforms list) is described in 1941 as about 0.1 mile northeast of a 'forest ranger fire lookout tower' on NC 171, 5.3 miles northeast of Mineola. That description does not name Foreman, and the mark was not found in 1963 or 2006.
